content: CPU/battery for laptop watchers: every poll is a CPU wake and wakes (not compute) dominate battery drain - frequent timers prevent deep sleep. Event-driven observers (FSEvents/inotify/kqueue) = zero wakes until real change; watchdog PollingObserver is 'slow and not recommended' (official docs) but REQUIRED for network mounts (NFS/CIFS/AFP - FSEvents/kqueue/inotify do not deliver events there; SIF-specific: iCloud/Dropbox-synced note dirs can silently miss events). watchdog v7 exposes FSEvents latency kwarg (was hard-coded 10ms; raising coalesces duplicates). PollingObserver emits DirDeletedEvent and STOPS when root unreadable via OSError in some cases; ENOENT outage looks like deletion. Patterns: adaptive backoff when quiet, battery-aware intervals, coalesce timers. Also watchdog v7: BaseThread always daemon threads; FileClosedEvent only on InotifyObserver(Linux); inotify missing root raises FileNotFoundError from schedule/start (#1157); FSEvents free-threading per-emitter streams (#1140). Sources: watchdog v7.1.0 PyPI changelog, watchdog polling docs, SO network-mount answers, AgentMonitors issue 469 power design.
